title: Check if it is Possible to Split Array
statement:
You get an array `nums` of length `n` and an integer `m`. Call an array *good* when it has exactly one element or its elements add up to at least `m`.

Start with `nums` as a single piece. In one move, pick any piece of length 2 or more and cut it into a non-empty left part and a non-empty right part; the move is allowed only if both parts are good. Return `true` if some sequence of moves ends with `n` pieces of length one, and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

A brute force tries every cut of every piece with an interval DP in O(n³), but the whole question collapses to one check. Whenever `n >= 3`, some move must eventually create a piece of exactly two neighbouring elements (follow the longer half of each cut downwards), and that piece is only good if the pair adds up to at least `m`. Conversely, if some neighbouring pair `nums[i], nums[i + 1]` reaches `m`, peel single elements off the two ends one at a time: every remaining piece still contains that pair, so its sum is at least `m` and the cut is allowed, and a lone element is always good. Arrays of length 1 or 2 need no long pieces at all.

## Approach

1. If `nums` has at most two elements, return `true`: every cut produces single elements.
2. Scan each neighbouring pair `nums[i]`, `nums[i + 1]`.
3. If a pair sums to at least `m`, return `true`.
4. If no pair does, return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 2, 1]`, `m = 4`. The length is 3, so scan pairs: `i = 0` gives `2 + 2 = 4 >= 4`, so the answer is `true`. Indeed, cutting off `[1]` leaves `[2, 2]` with sum 4, which then splits into two singles.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over neighbouring pairs.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Arrays of length 1 or 2 are always splittable, even when no sum reaches `m`.
- Only pairs of neighbours matter; the largest two values elsewhere in the array do not help.
- Checking the whole array's sum against `m` is not enough: a long piece can be good while every pair inside it is too small, and then a two-element piece eventually fails.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the array to split |
| `m` | the minimum sum a piece longer than one needs |
| `i` | index of the left element of the current neighbouring pair |

narration.2: With one or two elements, every cut yields single elements, which are always good.
narration.5: Look at every pair of neighbouring elements.
narration.6: Does this pair reach m? Then it can be the last two-element piece.
narration.7: Peel elements off both ends around this pair; every piece keeps the pair, so every cut is allowed.
narration.10: No pair reaches m, so the unavoidable two-element piece can never be good.
